Mesh lines over surfaces

Source: R/edges-3d.R
edges_3d.Rd

edges_3d() draws the edges of a surface's cells over its faces, passed as the edges argument of a surface or mesh layer, or to coord_3d() for every such layer that sets none. The cells of a surface on a grid (geom_surface_3d(), the surface stats, geom_parametric_3d(), geom_spatraster_3d()) are the quadrilaterals between neighbouring grid points, so the lines run along the grid and leave out the diagonals that split each cell into triangles; the cells of a mesh are its polygons; a Delaunay surface has triangles as cells. every keeps every n-th grid line and the last one, as the strides of matplotlib's plot_surface() or Mathematica's Mesh -> n thin a dense mesh. The lines are strokes of the scene, hidden by nearer surfaces like any other line.

Usage

edges_3d(
  type = c("cells", "triangles"),
  every = 1L,
  colour = "white",
  linewidth = 0.2,
  linetype = 1,
  alpha = 0.6,
  hidden = c("hide", "dashed", "show")
)

Arguments

type

"cells" for the edges of the cells, "triangles" for every triangle edge.

every

Positive integer stride of the grid lines: one value for both directions or two, for the lines along x (or u) and along y (or v). A stride above 1 needs a surface on a grid.

colour, linewidth, linetype, alpha

Stroke of the lines.

hidden

Hidden stroke policy of the lines: "hide", "dashed" or "show".

Value

An edges specification for the edges argument of geom_surface_3d(), geom_mesh_3d(), the surface stats and coord_3d().

Details

Thin light lines with some transparency over a dark fill trace the grid without hiding the shading; dark lines over a light fill give the look of MATLAB's surf().

See also

outline_3d() for silhouettes, creases and boundary lines.

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 36), y = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 36))
d$z <- with(d, exp(-(x^2 + y^2)))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E", shading = "smooth", edges = edges_3d()) +
  coord_3d()
# \donttest{
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "grey90", shading = "smooth") +
  coord_3d(edges = edges_3d(every = 5, colour = "grey20", alpha = 1),
           outline = outline_3d(silhouette = FALSE, crease = NULL))
# }
